The eighth: He, exalted is He, possesses singularity (fardaniyyah), in which no association is valid, neither in ownership (milk, with a kasra on the mim), nor in dominion (mulk, with a damma), nor in management, nor in influence.

The ninth: He, exalted is He, possesses greatness (kibriya'), which precludes the loss of a perfection or the perfection of a perfection.

The tenth: He, exalted is He, possesses might ('izzah), which precludes that He have an opposite, who is one who corrupts what He does, or a rival, who is one who brings into existence the like of what He brings into existence.

It is clear how these ten apply to the surah for whoever contemplates the speech and reflects upon it. He, glory be to Him, began the surah with the pronoun before the noun, after the explicit mention of victory, conquest, and the ruin of the disbelievers through the ruin of Abu Lahab, who was the highest and most honored of them, as an indication that whoever purifies his inner self with the name of Allah, exalted is He, is granted victory and conquest, as the command at the end of Surat al-Baqarah indicates, with the call to Him for victory over the disbelievers, by His saying:

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 112, verse 4 (part 2 of 4):

﴿Allah, there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence﴾ [al-Baqarah: 255]. Indeed, it is a translation of the beginning of this surah, which follows the surah of Victory (al-Nasr), and "al-Kafirun" (the Disbelievers) are equal with the pronoun and with the Greatest Name [and the Greatest Monotheism -], those who affirm by evidence, which is the quality of being self-subsisting (al-qayyumiyyah). It has clarified the end of the surah, which is its outcome, and has returned its conclusion to its opening: that He is One, ever present in every time, never absent at all, and no one is equal to Him or resembles Him, because nothing was begotten from Him, nor was He begotten from anything, for He is al-Samad (the Eternal Refuge), having no hollow at all, neither in His essence in actuality, nor in any manner that imagination could allow, because He is the One who encompasses everything, for He is Allah, who encompasses all the attributes of perfection and beauty. He is pure unseen, for no one else is able to know Him except through the necessary attributes that can be grasped by the intellect, approximately, and through the observable acts whose effects are seen. He is the One who, [He -] - despite being the Unseen of the Unseen - is present in every heart of understanding. He is never hidden from anyone by His effects, which have filled the regions. For this reason He deserved to be named by "Huwa" (He), and no other deserved it, because He is present in every heart and everything else is absent in every respect, since for other than Him, from its own essence, there is nothing but absence through non-existence. As for Him, He is the One whose existence is necessary. He is the One who brought others into existence and placed in [every -] drop of their remembrance (of Him), because of His perfection, glory be to Him, and because of others' great need for Him and their dependence. So He is Subbuh (Most Glorified) and Quddus (Most Holy), combining the two descriptions, for He is praised for virtues and excellences. Sanctification (taqdis) is implicit in the explicit glorification (tasbih), and glorification is implicit in the explicit sanctification. Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, has combined the two in this surah through the names whose manifestation began with its beginning. So He is explicit sanctification, and from there to its end is explicit glorification. Both matters return to His singling out, His unity, and the negation of partnership and likeness from Him. That is the combination of affirmation and negation, to stir up what occurred in the word of sincere devotion (kalimat al-ikhlas), so that it is known that affirmation is not perfected except by safeguarding Him from everything that would imply opposition to Him. However, the word of sincere devotion is composed of negation and then affirmation, while the surah of Sincerity (surat al-Ikhlas) is of affirmation and then negation. So its beginning is affirmation and its end is negation, and the end of affirmation is al-Samad, which combines the two matters, for it is the gathering of every attribute without which creation cannot be completed. [For] one of its two meanings in the language is: the lord to whom one returns. That requires affirming the attributes of perfection by which the coherence of acts is completed, and negating every attribute from which He is exalted. For the second of its two meanings in the language is: the one who has no hollow, and that includes negation of limit, negation of boundary, direction, body, and substance. For whoever is described by any of these would not be permitted to be described as composite or as having a hollow. Thus this word establishes the obligation of knowledge through negation and affirmation, so that truth may be distinguished from falsehood, for whoever does not verify the purity of falsehood will not have knowledge of the truth firmly established for him. For this reason the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them all, used to ask the Prophet ﷺ about the truth, for soundness of belief and knowledge, and about falsehood and evil, to be able to avoid it. Until "Hudhayfah, may Allah be pleased with him, said: 'People used to ask the Prophet ﷺ about good, and I used to ask him about evil.'" That is because whoever does not know evil is close to falling into it. And the word of testimony (kalimat al-shahadah) differs in order, because that one came for entry into the religion, while the more fitting for one who is outside it or weak in it, and they are the majority, is first to negate falsehood and erase it from the tablet of the heart, so that the affirmation of truth may come into it while it is empty, and it will settle therein. So when it first negated every other, which was a cause of withdrawal and distance from the presences of holiness, then the Most Holy Essence and the Most Noble, Most Precious Name affirmed Him, the surah of Sincerity emphasized (this) for it is for the perfect ones who have acquired character by what precedes it of surahs. This affirmation is when it is recalled and the beauty of His effects is witnessed. Then it is concluded with the negation of others, so that by that the end of lives is manifested, upon returning to the effects, by presentation to the One, the Subduer.

And this surah has clarified that it is a path between creation and command. So when He opened creation with the ambiguous (mutashabih) creation of Adam, peace be upon him, because the ambiguous is what does not go beyond its forms, and its four divisions were concluded with the ambiguous creation of Jesus, peace be upon him, as has preceded at ﴿Indeed, Allah has chosen﴾ [Al 'Imran: 33] in Al 'Imran, which is the counterpart of this surah. Therefore, after the Mother of the Book (Umm al-Kitab), He opened the command with the ambiguous disjointed letters, and He concluded it, apart from the two protective surahs (al-Mu'awwidhatayn), which are in the state of departure, like the introduction. The opening with seeking refuge is for the Mother of the Book with an ambiguous surah, which is the surah of Sincerity. The ambiguity of its beginning was ambiguous from all its aspects; it does not enable anyone to say about it a statement that is definitively established or a probable opinion of strong likelihood. The ambiguity of its end does not satisfy with less than certainty at its beginning, regarding what we are charged to do in this abode, and it is the foundations of religion. Beyond that is what none of the righteous nor the near ones can grasp, and it is the Most Holy Essence. So whoever raises the ambiguity of creation above its rank has disbelieved, and whoever lowers the ambiguity of command from its exalted rank has disbelieved. And He made its end clearer than its beginning in some respects, as an indication of the elevation of the one granted success in his matter, and that in the end he will be clearer in unveiling and more evident in knowledge. He followed it with seeking refuge, as an indication of asking for protection in his affair, and complete preservation in the arena of his recognition. And He repeated it with duality, for the sake of encompassing the two matters, the outward and the inward, and for emphasis, as an alert to the difficulty of the aim and the gravity of the station.

When the Qur'an opened with a surah that comprises all its meanings, it concluded with two surahs whose meaning is included in it, which is seeking refuge, and whose mention is recommended throughout its parts and structures. In this there is another very great subtlety: when [the one who recites] knew by sincerity complete knowledge and the manifestation of religion in this supreme way, and thereby attained the utmost joy, and completion in this abode signals deficiency, the two protective surahs came to repel the evil of that.

The discussion of the treasures of the meanings of the surah of Sincerity, as Allah facilitated, has concluded according to its composition, arrangement, and order. What remains is the discussion of what Allah opened of its secrets in indicating the purpose of the surah, by considering its words individually: apparent nouns and pronouns, then its letters. In it, among the Most Beautiful Names and the Highest Attributes, upon which it founded its structure and on which its pillars are based, there are five, which are the ten words of the Verse of the Throne (Ayat al-Kursi), just as the obligatory prayers are five, and they are fifty in the Mother of the Book ("the good deed is rewarded tenfold"). Among the subtle indications is that they are like the five pillars of religion. So the pronoun indicates the rectification of the heart's inner state through faith, and soundness of intention and submission, until the structure of worship stands. The Greatest Name indicates that this rectification is for the sake of devotion (ta'alluh) through humility before the True God, by recalling His Greatest Name, just as prayer is the greatest of bodily acts of worship. This is for preparation for entering into worship. Then entering into it has as a condition the singleness of orientation (uhdiyyat al-tawajjuh), verifying sincerity in the soundness of the resolve upon it, just as zakat is that which confirms faith. That unity within unity is for the sake of sincerity in devotion, by what the repetition of the Greatest Name indicates, as is the condition of the disheveled, dusty pilgrim, stripped bare. That devotion is by recalling the servant's need of the Worshipped One and his inclination toward destruction in every respect, because he is hollow, and the absolute self-sufficiency of the Worshipped One is indicated by the relational name al-Samad, as is the condition of the fasting person in his worship, recalling his insignificance and great need, and the majesty of his Lord and His exaltation in His self-sufficiency. Whoever has these five pillars sound, his worship is at the highest peak of acceptance. Otherwise, it has only the name of attainment without much yield. And Allah is the Granter of success. That it is fifteen words is an indication that in the fifteenth year of prophethood they will know, by the overwhelming of His subjugation and the might of His authority, and His support for the oppressed of His party, and His strengthening of them in the Battle of Badr in the second year of the Hijrah, that the One who sent it has no equal, with a knowledge of witnessing that no one can deny or repel, so the proof of sincerity stands, and there is no escape. And if you add to them the obligatory hidden pronoun in "Qul" (Say), they become sixteen, indicating that in the sixteenth year of prophethood, which is the third year of the Hijrah, in the Battle of Uhud, the Manifest will be the Inward Name of Allah (al-Batin). For in it there was the calamity described in the biographies in detail, namely the killing of seventy of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, among them Hamzah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, may Allah be pleased with him, the uncle of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the lion of His Messenger ﷺ. That was after the Prophet ﷺ had manifestly prevailed in the early part of the day, to the extent that the disbelievers were defeated, without doubt in it, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And Allah had already fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing them by His permission, until when you lost courage and disputed﴾ [Al 'Imran: 152] - and the verses. Then Allah concealed that in the removal of the disbelievers during the day, and the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, were routed, until there remained with the Prophet ﷺ from among them only a very small number. The most that has been reported about their number is that they were close to forty, and he ﷺ remained steadfast with them in the face of the enemy, who were about three thousand, among them two hundred horsemen, who attacked and assaulted them, sometimes encircling him and sometimes separating from him, so that it would be known that the Helper is only Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, alone. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, said: "The Prophet ﷺ was never helped in any battlefield as he was helped at the Battle of Uhud." And Abu Sufyan ibn Harb said on the day of his Islam, in the year of the Conquest, to the Prophet ﷺ: "I never fought you once but that you prevailed over me. I think that if there were with Allah another, it would have availed nothing."

[Page 397] But what became manifest from it was what occurred at the end of the day, the victory of the disbelievers. God Most High concealed His support for His Prophet (ﷺ) in it through His hidden Name, known only to those endowed with insight. Thus no one knew this except through a very subtle correspondence with the inner pronoun, which must remain concealed. When you add to that the two hidden pronouns that may also be made manifest, the words total eighteen. This indicates that in the eighteenth year of prophethood, which is the fifth year of the Hijra, there is a great sign that He has no equal, one that necessitates sincere devotion (ikhlas) in a manner clearer than what occurred at the Battle of Uhud, even though that event also had some degree of obscurity. This refers to the Battle of the Confederates (al-Ahzab) and the Banu Qurayza, when God turned back the disbelievers in their rage, and they gained no good, although they had been ten thousand fighters apart from the Banu Qurayza. They were saying that there was no one who could overcome them. God sufficed the believers in fighting. ﴿And God was Strong and Mighty﴾ [33:25], subduing them by a wind and by hosts that they did not see ﴿And We sent against them hosts you did not see﴾ [33:9], and He gave the believers power over the Banu Qurayza. ﴿And God was Strong and Mighty﴾. This took place in Shawwal and Dhu al-Qa'da of the fifth year of the Hijra. When you add to these the other pronoun that is manifest in act, in the word ﴿lahu﴾ [His], the total is nineteen. This indicates a similar matter, in a manner clearer [...] at the 'Umra of al-Hudaybiyya in Dhu al-Qa'da of the sixth year of the Hijra. In it occurred the causal victory (al-fath al-sababi), for which God, glorified and exalted, sent down the Surah of Victory (al-Fath). In it there were many signs of God's oneness that necessitate sincere devotion, although there was a degree of obscurity in that, corresponding to the pronoun, even though it was manifest in act. Many of the Companions, may God be pleased with them all, did not perceive it until the Prophet (ﷺ) drew their attention to it. When you add to these the four words of the basmala, the total is twenty-three, corresponding to the tenth year of the Hijra, which is the twenty-third year of prophethood. In it the great victory was established and the greatest sincere devotion came about, by negating polytheism and its people from the Arabian Peninsula, at the Farewell Pilgrimage, of which the Prophet (ﷺ) said: [«Indeed, Satan has despaired of being worshipped in the land of the Arabs»]. For this reason, God Most High took His Prophet (ﷺ) after it, once the religion had been made manifest, the disbelievers humiliated, and the blessing completed. Glorified is He, Who alone undertook the support of the community after having prepared the means of victory through His Prophet (ﷺ). He knew with certainty, amid the apostasy (ridda) and its conditions, the surging of strife and its horrors, the dominance of its terror over hearts and its tremors, in that severe turmoil, that He is the God alone, who has no equal, in preserving the religion during the life of His Prophet (ﷺ) and after him. Likewise in what followed of the conquests of lands and the humbling of stubborn, fierce kings, despite their great numbers, strength, wealth, forces, and great power in the lands. He made the victory over them come through the people of weakness and few numbers, [page 399] a sign within a sign, and a proof extremely manifest in its clarity. If you follow another method of arrangement in the written and conventional words, it indicates a similar matter by another way. This is that you add to the fifteen words the four words of the basmala, making nineteen, which corresponds to the sixth year of the Hijra, the year of the 'Umra of al-Hudaybiyya, which God called a victory (fath), and in which He sent down the Surah of Victory, because it was the cause of the victory which is the pillar of sincere devotion. When you add to them the hidden pronoun, the total is twenty, corresponding to the seventh year, in which was the 'Umra of the Qada' (Umrat al-Qada'). In it God made manifest the sincere devotion [to Him] for His servant and Messenger (ﷺ) among the polytheists, in the city from which he was sent, and in which there appeared, in a manner, that He has no equal. Yet this occurred in a hidden manner. When you add to them the two hidden pronouns that may become manifest, the total is twenty-two, corresponding to the ninth year, the Year of Delegations (sanat al-wufud), when people entered the religion of God in multitudes. The divinity (al-ilahiyya), insofar as it is divinity, requires unity, but unity does not require divinity. He expressed it with [al-Ahad] rather than [al-Wahid], because the intent is to emphasize the attribute of unity to a degree beyond which nothing could be greater. Ibn Sina said: "The one (al-wahid) is predicated of what falls under it by gradation (al-tashkik). That which is not divisible in any respect at all is more worthy of oneness than that which is divisible in some respects. That which is divisible by rational division is more worthy than that which is divisible by sense, and that which is divisible by sense in potentiality is more worthy than that which is divisible by sense in actuality." When it is established that unity admits of greater and lesser degrees, and that the one is predicated of what falls under it by gradation, [then] the most perfect in act is that which cannot have anything else stronger than it in that respect, for otherwise it would not reach the utmost goal. Al-Ahad comprises all of this and indicates oneness in every respect, and that there is no multiplicity there at all, neither a notional multiplicity of the predicables, such as genera and differentiae, nor by rational parts such as matter and form, nor a multiplicity by sense, whether potential or actual, as is found in bodies. This is because He, glorified and exalted, is free of genus, differentia, matter, form, accidents, parts, organs, shapes, colors, and all aspects of resemblance that would mar the complete, true unity, which is befitting of the nobility of His Face and the might of His majesty, that anything should resemble Him or equal Him. For whatever's identity is to be obtained from the combination of another [thing], its identity is dependent upon those parts, and so it is not He Himself in Himself, but in another. Therefore He is free of multiplicity in every respect and characterized by oneness in every aspect. This composition has reached the greatest level of eloquent expression. Glorified is He Who sent down this speech: how great is its rank, and how overpowering is His authority! He is the ultimate of needs, and from Him is the attainment of desires. The lowest of what He has reserved for Himself of majesty, greatness, and splendor cannot be reached by the utmost descriptions of those who describe, nor by the greatest attribute of those who attribute. Rather, the possible measure of that, and what is impossible beyond it, is what He mentioned in His Mighty Book, and deposited in His holy and wise revelation. By speaking about its meaning and the one meaning, what has been previously stated is verified. The Imam Abu al-'Abbas al-Iqlishi said in his commentary on the Most Beautiful Names (al-Asma' al-Husna): "Whoever considers the language equates the two and makes them synonymous. Some say: the origin of 'Ahad' is 'Wahid,' from which the alif was dropped, then the hamza was substituted for the fathah-vowelled waw, like [hasan yahsunu fahuwa hasan], from al-husn; the waw was replaced by a hamza." As for those who differentiate between them: some say, "Ahad" stands on its own, with no substitution or change in it. Others say its origin is [wahad], with the waw replaced by a hamza. End.

I have summarized the discussion of the two noble names from several commentaries on the Most Beautiful Names and other works, including the commentary of al-Fakhr al-Razi and al-Fakhr al-Harrali and others. They said: The One (al-Wahid) is the one in whom there is no plurality in any respect, neither by division nor otherwise, together with His being described by greatness. This excludes the indivisible atom (al-jawhar al-fard, the particle that cannot be divided), which is that which cannot be doubled, meaning it has no opposite and no like. He, glorified and exalted is He, is One in both senses absolutely, not with regard to a state or to anything else.

Abu al-Abbas al-Iqlishi said in his commentary on the Most Beautiful Names: "This is the true meaning of unity according to the verifiers (al-muhaqqiqun). Thus nothing composite may be described by it except metaphorically, as you say: a man who is one (rajul wahid) and a dirham who is one (dirham wahid). It is properly predicated only of that which has no movement of its own (? like the jawhar according to the Ash'aris). However, when you consider and find that its existence comes from another, you know that its deserving of this attribute is not like the deserving of its Originator for it. It is also described by it only because of its lowliness, whereas its Originator, glorified and exalted is He, is described by it together with being described by greatness. So His being described by unity is absolute, while being described by the jawhar, with regard to the absence of composition from body, is accompanied by the correctness of its being described as a part, which removes from it the reality of that. Unity, too, with regard to the second sense, which is that which has no counterpart, is not correct in its true sense except for Him, glorified and exalted. Everything whose species is in its individual, such as the Throne, the Chair, the Sun and the Moon, can be supposed to have counterparts. It also has a third sense, which is unity in action and origination, so that He does whatever He wills without depending on anything. The difference between this aspect and the one before it is that the first looks at the negation of a second god, while this one negates a specific partner or minister. Both are essential negative attributes. The conclusion is that correct reasoning shows that we have one Originator, in the sense that no deficiency can reach Him by division in any way, and in the sense that He has no counterpart in any respect, and in the sense that He is independent in action, self-sufficient in origination, unique in making, and singular in governance. Witness of the intellect, protected from the darkness of desire and the density of nature, has decided this, and the decisive transmitted reports and the speaking hearing have confirmed it. For this reason, among the greatest of creatures is His supplication, glorified and exalted is He, for all creation, and the call of His Seal of the Messengers ﷺ was to all mankind."

Hujjat al-Islam Abu Hamid al-Ghazali said at the end of his commentary on the Most Beautiful Names, in his explanation of the return of the many names to the essence of the One and the seven attributes of the Unique (al-Ahad), from which the counterpart is negated, and he said in the aforementioned commentary: "The One is the one who is not divisible and not doubled. As for the one that is not divisible, it is like the jawhar that cannot be divided, so it is said of it that it is one, in the sense that it has no part. Likewise the point has no part. God, exalted is He, is One in the sense that it is impossible to suppose division in His essence. As for the one that is not doubled, it is the one that has no counterpart, like the sun for example, for it, although it is capable of division in imagination, is bounded in its essence because it belongs to the category of bodies. So it has no counterpart, except that a counterpart for it is possible. There is no existing thing in existence that is singular in the particular reality of its existence with a singularity such that no other can be conceived to share in it at all, except the absolutely One, from eternity to eternity. A servant is only one when he has no counterpart among the members of his kind in any one of the good qualities. This is relative to some qualities and not all of them. So there is no absolute unity except for God, glorified and exalted is He."

Muhammad ibn Abd al-Karim al-Shahrastani said in the introduction to the book Al-Milal wa al-Nihal (The Religions and the Sects): "They differed concerning the One: is it of the nothing, or the origin of number, and not included in number? This difference arises only from the stipulation of the word one as well. The one is used to mean that from which number is composed, for two has no meaning except one repeated for the first time, and likewise three and four. It is also used to mean that from which the number that is a cause results, and it is not included in the number that is not composed of it. All numbers may accompany oneness, not on the basis that number is composed by it, but rather every existing thing is its genus, its species or its individual, which is one. It is said: a person is one. And in number, He has no equal, but that was in a hidden way. If you add to these the two hidden pronouns that may be manifested, they become twenty-two, corresponding to the year nine, the year of the delegations and the entry of people into the religion in multitudes, and the pilgrimage of Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, and the purification of the Sacred Mosque from the filth of polytheism by the disavowal of the polytheists, and prohibiting them from making the pilgrimage after that year, and the prohibition on them approaching the Sacred Mosque because they are impure, and the spread of sincerity in most of the lands of the Arabs. That is clearer than what has passed, is appropriate to what it indicates, and there is a kind of obscurity in it for those among the polytheists who remained. If you add to them the other pronoun, which is manifest in act, they become twenty-three, corresponding to the year of the Farewell Pilgrimage, the year ten, in which sincerity was completed, no polytheist made the pilgrimage, and Satan despaired that he would be worshipped in the Arabian Peninsula. In that, because the word is a pronoun, there is a slight kind of obscurity regarding what it indicated afterwards of apostasy. And that was the most fitting of things for the word that bears that pronoun, and it belongs to it. This is what Allah has disclosed of the secrets of its words according to the numbers. As for its letters, there is a great secret: that it is an attribute of Allah, and that its letters together with the basmala, considered in terms of pronunciation and likewise in terms of writing, are sixty-six letters, and likewise the number of the letters of the pronounced and written Name of Majesty (al-Jalalah) by the reckoning of the abjad (jummal). So everything it calls to is the meaning of this greatest Name. And if this count is taken from the beginning of the birth of the Prophet ﷺ, its last point coincides with the year of death of his greatest companion, who preceded others by what was lodged in his breast, Abu Bakr, may Allah the Exalted be pleased with him. That is an indication that no one equals these two in sincerity, and that both reached the highest rank in it, even though the Prophet ﷺ was the highest of creation in it. In this there is also an indication that He has no equal, because He negated polytheism entirely from the whole Arabian Peninsula after they had been unanimously upon it, and He released them, glorified and exalted is He, over those who were near them of the [kings of the] nations, until Allah made the religion, through them, prevail over all religion, though they had been the most humiliated of the nations, and they overthrew the tyrant kings with humiliation after they had believed that no one could overcome them. Its pronounced letters are equal to the number of [the words of] the verses of Oneness, and that is the Verse of the Throne, the greatest verse in the Qur'an, and that is fifty letters less one, which is the alif of ﴿equal﴾, which is written but not pronounced, and it indicates the pronoun that is the Hidden of the Hidden, so it is hidden from the aspect of not being pronounced, yet existent and manifest from the aspect of the witness of the written form and the heard Name, just as the Essence is a pure hidden from the aspect of reality, perceived through the witnessing of acts, and the heard lofty Names. And Allah is the Guide from error."
